name: RobustSpring
description: Standard benchmarks for optical flow, scene flow, and stereo vision algorithms generally focus on model accuracy rather than robustness to image corruptions like noise or rain. Hence, the resilience of models to such real-world perturbations is largely unquantified. To address this, we present RobustSpring, a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for evaluating robustness to image corruptions for optical flow, scene flow, and stereo models. RobustSpring applies 20 different image corruptions, including noise, blur, color changes, quality degradations, and weather distortions, in a time-, stereo-, and depth-consistent manner to the high-resolution Spring dataset, creating a suite of 20,000 corrupted images that reflect challenging conditions. RobustSpring enables comparisons of model robustness via a new corruption robustness metric. Integration with the Spring benchmark enables public two-axis evaluations of both accuracy and robustness. We benchmark a curated selection of initial models, observing that accurate models are not necessarily robust and that robustness varies widely by corruption type. RobustSpring is a new computer vision benchmark that treats robustness as a first-class citizen to foster models that combine accuracy with resilience. It will be available at https://spring-benchmark.org.
evaluation_method: standard accuracy metrics (e.g., End-Point Error) combined with a corruption robustness metric introduced by the benchmark
general_score_metric: corruption robustness metric (paired with standard accuracy such as EPE)
reputation: A recent robustness-focused extension of the Spring benchmark; intended for researchers evaluating vision models' resilience to realistic time/stereo-consistent corruptions.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark. Uses synthetic but time/stereo/depth-consistent corruptions applied to Spring data — realistic but not identical to arbitrary real-world noise. Large-scale (20k corrupted images) and compute-intensive for full evaluation; corruption-specific performance can vary widely, so single-number comparisons may hide details.
